title: Upcoming demand bounds Extend
lede: Booking Detail now keeps the checkout extension path available when gear is booked later, while making the next booking's start the explicit return boundary.

stats.n: The reservation turnaround buffer no longer consumes otherwise free time for an already-open checkout.
The same future booking remains visible in both captures.
The server still rejects any due time after the next booking starts.

sections.heading: Matched iPhone 16 Pro capture
sections.note: Same iOS 26.5 simulator, fixture booking, equipment, upcoming reservation, and viewport. Only the extension policy and its explanatory copy differ.

pairs.title: Open checkout with a later reservation
pairs.sub: The camera is due at 3:29 PM and booked again at 5:29 PM.
pairs.beforeCap: Upcoming demand declared the entire extension path unavailable.
pairs.afterCap: The next-needed time remains prominent, and Extend stays fixed at the bottom with that time as its hard boundary.

changes.h: Upcoming demand was treated as a categorical stop
changes.was: Any future serialized booking hid Extend for an open checkout, even when hours of conflict-free time remained.
changes.now: Upcoming demand constrains the selected return time. The checkout can extend up to the next booking's actual start.

changes.was: The shared 60-minute serialized buffer blocked the extension before a real overlap existed.
changes.now: Only this open-checkout extension path uses overlap-only serialized checks. Bulk shortages, true overlaps, optimistic freshness, serializable writes, audit history, and database overlap protection remain enforced.

verification: 94 focused Vitest checks pass across availability, extend/edit services, native source policy, and concurrency headers.
iPhone 16 Pro UI proof: the final XCTest asserts both upcoming-demand guidance and the visible Extend Return Date action.
Matched baseline: the same lowercase server-action fixture and iOS 26.5 destination reproduce the prior hidden-action behavior.
notes: Reservation creation and reservation editing still require the standard 60-minute serialized turnaround buffer.
The captures use deterministic local fixtures; authenticated production and deployed behavior are separate release gates.
